result.migration_review: Additive-only, single `add :join_counters, :map, null: false, default: %{}` column matching the already-shipped `variables` column idiom verbatim. `null: false, default: %{}` is safe against the design's own claim (re-confirmed by reading insert_instance_projection/8's own call site) that instance_projections has had live writers via create/2 since REQ-045 -- a DB-level default backfills every existing row atomically as part of the ALTER, no separate backfill migration needed for a scalar default. Tenant-scoped `if prefix() do` guard present; registered in TenantProvisioning's manifest (both the tuple entry and the migration's own guard, confirmed present). ELIXIR-DEV's own handoff attests migrate/rollback/migrate all ran clean in-session -- not independently re-run here (mix is not available in this review sandbox's PATH, confirmed: `which mix`/`type mix` both fail, no asdf/mise shims found) -- this is a toolchain gap in this review environment, not a finding against the change; flagging per core-directives rather than fabricating a run.
result.tenant_isolation_review: No cross-tenant read/write introduced. build_instance_state/3's new read is not a second Repo call at all -- it reads projection.join_counters off the exact %InstanceProjection{} struct already passed in as an argument (the one fetch_and_lock_instance_projection/3 locked earlier in the same transaction), confirmed by reading the function body: no repo/prefix argument exists on build_instance_state/3's signature, so there is no code path by which it could read a different tenant's or a different instance's row.
result.concurrency_test_review: test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs's 'concurrent sibling-branch completion' test (lines ~224-298) uses Elixir.Task.async/1 (two genuinely independent BEAM processes) + Elixir.Task.await_many/2, against a tenant provisioned via TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 which calls Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) (confirmed by reading test/support/tenant_fixture.ex line 191) -- :auto mode gives each spawned Task its own real Postgres connection rather than serializing them under shared sandbox ownership, so this is genuine concurrent execution on two distinct task_ids of the same instance, not two sequential calls dressed up. Assertions correctly avoid asserting which branch wins the M2 lock race (non-deterministic), only asserting the outcome (exactly one :completed, one :active, join_counters == %{} after both commit, both tasks :completed) -- matches the design's own §3.3/§5.2 correctness argument exactly. Not independently executed in this review sandbox (mix unavailable, see migration_review note); ELIXIR-DEV's handoff attests 2/2 passes across 3 repeated runs plus a full-suite run showing 3031/3033 passing with the only 2 failures being a pre-existing, unrelated rustc-toolchain gap.

create2_extension_assessment.verdict: IN-FAMILY, NOT SCOPE CREEP -- concur with ELIXIR-DEV's own self-flag
create2_extension_assessment.q1_same_mechanism: Yes, genuinely the same mechanism: same field (join_counters), same codec (SnapshotWriter.serialize_join_counters/1, the identical public function reconcile_projection/5 now calls), no new lock, no new table, no new transaction boundary. insert_instance_projection/8 is called from persist/12's own pre-existing Multi.run(:instance_projection, ...) step (engine.ex ~956-976) -- a Multi step that already existed and already inserted this same InstanceProjection row for every other column (status, current_nodes, variables); this change adds one more field to an attrs map an INSERT was already going to issue, exactly the same shape as reconcile_projection/5's own change to an UPDATE it was already going to issue.
create2_extension_assessment.q2_locking_discipline: Different code path, correctly so, and the design's concurrency argument does not need to apply to it. insert_instance_projection/8 runs inside a plain repo.insert(prefix: prefix) against a freshly-generated instance_id -- confirmed by reading persist/12's Multi.run(:instance_projection, ...) step and insert_instance_projection/8's body: this is instance creation, definitionally a brand-new row with no pre-existing sibling row for a concurrent transaction to race on (no other transaction can hold or contend for a FOR UPDATE lock on a row that does not exist until this INSERT commits). The design's §3.1-§3.3 concurrency argument is built entirely around fetch_and_lock_instance_projection/3's FOR UPDATE on an EXISTING row across separate complete_task/3/advance_after_timer_fired/3 calls -- that argument is simply inapplicable here, not violated, because create/2 is single-writer-by-construction for this row at this point in time. No new race is introduced by this extension.
create2_extension_assessment.q3_scope_check: Confirmed narrowly targeted: the only behavioral change is threading new_instance_state.join_counters (a value create/2's own hop-chain already computed in memory via the same Transition.transition/3 pure call the rest of the design already relies on) into the same INSERT's attrs map via the same serialize_join_counters/1 call. No new table, no new endpoint, no new external surface, no change to create/2's return shape or error handling. Directly closes ISS-0397's reported symptom for the one hop-chain shape (split immediately after START, within create/2's own initial dispatch) that the design's own §5.1/§5.3 test fixtures already exercise and that ELIXIR-DEV's regression test caught failing pre-fix (map_size(join_counters) == 0 immediately after Engine.create/2). Documented transparently: flagged in the ELIXIR-DEV handoff's routing note, in an engine.ex code comment at the call site, and in a new docs/anti-patterns.md entry -- not silently added.
create2_extension_assessment.recommendation_for_reviewer: REVIEWER should confirm from an OTP-idiom/design-process-integrity angle that this warrants only a rework-note (anti-patterns entry, already added) rather than sending the design doc itself back for a rework cycle -- SECURITY-REVIEWER's own assessment is that a design-rework cycle is not warranted here since the fix is mechanically identical to the approved design, but that call also sits partly in REVIEWER's lane (scope-creep/process-integrity gate).

result.req052_coordination_check: Confirmed cancel_instance/3 and cancel_instance_projection/4 are untouched: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine.ex | grep 'cancel_instance'` returns zero hits. ELIXIR-DEV correctly left REQ-052's decision-record-drift observation (its cited blocker -- 'the join-counters persistence gap' -- is now gone) as a flag for ORCH in its own handoff routing note rather than unilaterally wiring {:cancel_branch, _} through cancel_instance/3. No action needed from SECURITY-REVIEWER beyond confirming the non-change; this is an ORCH/decision-record item, not a security defect.
result.hygiene_check: No secrets in any changed file. No scope creep beyond ISS-0397 plus the one flagged in-family create/2 extension (the req208_meridian_test.exs rewrite is a necessary consequence of the fix changing prior-broken assertions to now-correct ones, and its own incidentally-found task-ordering issue is documented in-place, not silently introduced as unrelated behavior).
result.summary: PASS. All applicable invariants (INV-1, INV-4, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8) verified against the real diff with no findings. INV-2/3/5 correctly NOT-APPLICABLE (pre-S4/S5). The create/2 insert_instance_projection/8 extension beyond the design's literal text is genuinely in-family: same field, same codec, no new lock/table/transaction boundary, and the design's concurrency argument simply does not need to apply to a fresh-row INSERT with no concurrent sibling. Routing to REVIEWER (Step 3d) for OTP-idiom/scope-creep/decision-record-consistency review, with explicit attention requested on the create/2 extension (assessed above) and the still-open REQ-052 decision-record-drift flag (an ORCH item, not a REVIEWER action item, but relevant context).
